To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a new framework, MELR, for few-shot learning that is based on the modeling of episode-level relationships; (2) our MELR is the first to show that the inter-episode relationships can improve the robustness of few-shot learning models against poorly-sampled shots; and (3) extensive experiments on two benchmarks show the effectiveness of the proposed MELR framework.

1) by exploiting inter-episodic relationships, the proposed framework can improve the robustness of FSL against the poor sampling of training instances; 2) the proposed MELR framework can be easily extended to the transductive FSL setting, which can be used to improve the performance of state-of-the-art methods by 2.2%-5.0%.

(i) the proposed MELR framework can improve the performance of FSL by modeling inter-episode relationships; (ii) the proposed MCEAM and MCECR can effectively alleviate the effect of poorly-sampled instances and enforce the consistency between the two classifiers, respectively.
